plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($47), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay only that second-highest bid—maximizing my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win but the second-highest bid exceeds my true value. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly $47.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. My value is $33, so I will bid $33 to maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price auction, so bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly $36 ensures I win whenever the second-highest bid is below my value (guaranteeing positive profit) and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding higher than 36 risks paying more than my value if I "win" against someone bidding between 36 and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, $36 is optimal.
